title: How much ribbon does each of four friends get?
description: The same twenty nine metre ribbon is shared equally among four friends. Twenty nine over four is changed to a fraction with a hundred below, because four times twenty five is a hundred. Keeko's doubt is that seven metres with one left over is seven point one metres.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the bottom is not a factor of ten, look for a hundred or a thousand and multiply the top and the bottom by the same number. Watch for students who write a remainder of one as zero point one.

source: The same 29 m ribbon is shared equally among 4 friends. How
video_script.why: The child has turned halves into tenths but has not met a bottom that does not go into ten.
video_script.substitution: Four times twenty five is a hundred, so twenty nine quarters become seven hundred and twenty five hundredths.
video_script.anchor: The same twenty nine metre red ribbon is shared equally among four friends
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko writes seven metres with one left over as seven point one metres, but one metre in four parts is a quarter, not a tenth.
video_script.payoff_line: Each friend gets seven point two five metres of ribbon.
video_script.fraction_reading: A fraction such as 29/4 is read twenty nine over four, and 725/100 is read seven hundred and twenty five over a hundred.
maths_rules: 4 is not a factor of 10, but 4 x 25 = 100
video_script.design: The ribbon stays on the board all video; the working band turns twenty nine quarters into hundredths and reads them as a decimal.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a red ribbon labelled 29 m; three cut marks split it among four friends

marks.ribbon: the red ribbon appears with its length
marks.share: cut marks split the ribbon among four friends
marks.ask: a question mark glows over one share

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is an example from your book about a red ribbon.
<bookmark mark='ribbon'/>The ribbon is red, and it is twenty nine metres long.
<bookmark mark='share'/>Then the whole ribbon is shared equally among four friends.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How much ribbon does each friend get?

beats.on_screen: the ribbon and the question stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 10 does not split into 4 equal whole parts; 100 splits into 4 groups of 25

marks.ten: a row of ten squares cannot be split into four equal whole groups
marks.hundred: a grid of a hundred squares splits into four groups of twenty five

narration: <bookmark mark='ten'/>Four is not a factor of ten. Ten squares cannot be split into four equal whole groups.
<bookmark mark='hundred'/>Four is a factor of a hundred. A hundred squares make four groups of twenty five.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Four times twenty five is a hundred, so we can use hundredths.

beats.on_screen: Given: red ribbon 29 m; shared equally among 4 friends

marks.given: the ribbon length and the four friends are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a red ribbon is twenty nine metres long. It is shared equally among four friends.

beats.on_screen: To find: length of ribbon each friend gets

marks.find: the length of one share is outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the length of ribbon each friend gets.
<bookmark mark='s1a'/>Step one, write the share as a division. Each friend gets twenty nine divided by four metres.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>As a fraction, that is twenty nine over four.
<bookmark mark='s2a'/>Step two, make the bottom a hundred. Four times twenty five is a hundred.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Multiply the top and the bottom by twenty five, so the fraction stays equal.
<bookmark mark='s3a'/>Step three, find the new top. Twenty nine times twenty five is seven hundred and twenty five.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>The share is seven hundred and twenty five over a hundred.

marks.s4a: 725 hundredths is split into 7 Ones and 25 Hundredths

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Step four, read it as a decimal. Seven hundred and twenty five hundredths is seven Ones and twenty five Hundredths.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>We write the seven, the point, and then the twenty five.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Each friend gets seven point two five metres of ribbon.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the ribbon
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 7 m with 1 m left, written 7.1; a metre cut into four quarters sits beside a tenth; the bubble is crossed out

marks.fix: a metre cut into four quarters is placed beside a metre cut into ten
marks.right: one quarter is written as 25 hundredths

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks seven metres with one left over is seven point one metres.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But zero point one is one tenth of a metre. A metre shared among four gives a quarter, which is bigger than a tenth.
<bookmark mark='right'/>A quarter of a metre is twenty five hundredths. Each friend gets seven point two five metres.
